punchline: Howard Hughes's defense business only began to thrive after he handed it to someone else.
thirty_sec: Howard Hughes inherited three quarters of his father's tool company at eighteen and bought out his relatives. Over the years he lost fortunes on stocks, films, a plane that flew once for barely a mile, and a studio. Yet the defense business he finally handed to executives began to do well, because he was no longer in it. Ryan Holiday's verdict is short: ego wrecked him.
